burdens.eyebrow: Where a marketing Work Agent earns its place
burdens.title: Keep positioning and creative judgment human. Delegate the production trail.
burdens.description: Marketing work fragments when audience evidence, approved claims, channel drafts, review feedback, and performance data live in separate production loops.

items.label: Context
items.title: Audience evidence is separated from creative work
items.description: Interview notes, search behavior, sales calls, support themes, and analytics rarely travel with the creative brief they should inform.

items.label: Format
items.title: Every channel needs a new format
items.description: A campaign idea must become email, social, landing-page, sales, and regional variants without losing the approved message.

items.label: Coordination
items.title: Review feedback is hard to reconcile
items.description: Product, legal, brand, regional, and channel feedback arrives in different places and often refers to different draft versions.

items.label: Continuity
items.title: Performance reporting repeats every cycle
items.description: Data is exported again, campaign context is reconstructed, and the original hypothesis gets separated from the final results.

workflows.eyebrow: Three assignments for a marketing Work Agent
workflows.title: Delegate campaign preparation without delegating positioning or publication.
workflows.description: Each assignment starts from approved research, claims, and data, returns editable assets, and stops before budget, targeting, attribution, or publishing decisions.

items.title: Build a campaign brief from evidence
items.job: Turn research, product context, constraints, and objectives into a shared plan before asset production.
items.output: A campaign brief with claims, channels, measures, and open questions.
items.boundary: Marketing owners approve positioning, claims, budget, and success criteria.

items.title: Adapt approved content across channels
items.job: Create channel-specific drafts from one approved source while preserving message and brand constraints.
items.output: Editable email, social, landing-page, and sales-support drafts.
items.boundary: Humans verify claims, permissions, tone, and every publication decision.

items.title: Prepare a performance review
items.job: Combine approved campaign data with the original hypothesis to explain changes and next questions.
items.output: A performance summary, experiment log, and next-step options.
items.boundary: The growth team validates attribution and decides budget or strategy changes.

boundaries.title: Let the Work Agent prepare assets. Keep claims, strategy, and publication human-owned.
boundaries.description: The Work Agent may prepare evidence-backed briefs, variants, and reviews; it cannot invent claims, select audiences or budgets, confirm attribution, or publish on the team's behalf.
boundaries.assistsTitle: The Work Agent can help prepare
assists: Campaign briefs linking audience evidence, objectives, approved claims, and open questions
Channel-specific drafts derived from one approved source asset
Claim and message checks that point reviewers back to supporting evidence
Feedback summaries that preserve reviewer, version, and unresolved conflicts

boundaries.note: Floatboat is a general-purpose Work Agent, not a marketing automation or publishing platform. Its workspace connects approved evidence, tools, instructions, feedback, and drafts; marketing owners retain claims, budget, targeting, and publication decisions.

faq.title: Work Agent questions for marketers and growth teams
faq.description: Marketing teams need to scale adaptation without inventing claims, losing approvals, confusing attribution, or flattening every channel into the same copy.

items.question: Is Floatboat a marketing automation or publishing platform?
items.answer: No. Your CRM, analytics, ad, email, and CMS tools remain the systems of record and distribution. Floatboat helps prepare the research, briefs, variants, and review artifacts that move between them.

items.question: Can it choose positioning or launch a campaign on its own?
items.answer: It can organize evidence and draft strategic options, but marketing owners decide the audience, positioning, claims, budget, channel mix, and publication plan.

items.question: Can it follow our brand voice and approved claims?
items.answer: Yes. Supply the current message house, style rules, claim evidence, prohibited language, channel requirements, and approval path for the campaign.

items.question: How do we stop AI from inventing product claims?
items.answer: Restrict drafting to approved product sources and claim libraries, require evidence beside factual assertions, flag unsupported language, and keep product or legal review where the campaign requires it.

items.question: Can customer research or campaign data be used?
items.answer: Only when consent, contracts, policy, and applicable privacy rules permit it. Prefer aggregated or de-identified inputs and check how every selected model and connector handles the data.

items.question: Will it publish channel variants automatically?
items.answer: The recommended workflow keeps every asset as an editable draft until the appropriate owner approves the claim, creative, audience, destination, and timing.

items.question: What is a useful first marketing workflow?
items.answer: Take one approved campaign brief and source asset, generate two channel-specific drafts, and review message fidelity and channel fit before expanding the workflow.
